failures: PR-0009 NOT FIXED (major, both games). The critic's acceptance check — 'the panel's bottom edge equals a measured line bottom to within 1 px and the chip's box intersects no glyph' — fails at every viewport tested, live, PYREFLY_BROWSER=gpu (mode reported by tools/browser-mode.mjs as 'gpu'), real keyboard input via critic/rounds/round-04/r4-flow.mjs, dev server on :5194. Measured with one Range per text node (true glyph line boxes, no block-container rects). FFX Chapter 1, 1600x900: stage scale 2.5057; panel content bottom 275.02 px; nearest glyph line bottom 8.65 px away (3.45 unscaled stage units, i.e. ~3.5x the 1 px tolerance); 1 sliced line — 'Haste is ctb x 8/16 - roughly...' occupies 271.21-286.21 so only 3.8 px of its 15 px box is inside the panel; MORE chip box 252.50-280.00 intersects 2 glyph line boxes. FFX Chapter 1, 2000x1012 (Bailey's own size): scale 2.8175; content bottom 309.99; gap 10.48 px (3.72 stage units); 1 sliced line (304.96-321.83); chip 283.92-314.84 intersects 2 glyph boxes. FFX-2 Chapter 4, 1600x900: scale 2.5072; content bottom 459.27; gap 8.37 px (3.34 units); chip 437.50-465.00 intersects the visible 'Watch' heading line box 435.90-450.90. FFX-2 Chapter 4, 2000x1012: scale 2.8191; gap 10.16 px (3.60 units); chip 491.94-522.86 intersects 'Watch' 490.14-507.01. The screenshot crops show it directly: in FFX the third body line is cut through and MORE is drawn over it; in FFX-2 the WATCH section heading is cut and MORE sits on the same band. The currentScale() unit conversion is right in principle and the new unit test proves the arithmetic, but it is a jsdom test that mocks exactly the rect = scale x offsetHeight relationship the fix assumes, so it cannot catch this; the residual ~3.4 stage-unit error is a second, un-diagnosed term (the chip's height is still overlaid rather than reserved in the body's max-height, which the critic's own fix text asked for as the second half: 'Reserve the chip's height in the body's max-height instead of overlaying it'). Steps to reproduce: dev server, chapter select -> Chapter I (or Chapter IV), Enter through prep and the pre-battle scene, wait for a command row, press G, then measure .sgd__panel's content-box bottom against per-text-node Range.getClientRects() bottoms inside .sgd__body and against .sgd__more's rect.

PR-0009 acceptance was reported as blocked by a battle-flow stall that does not exist. The guide commit (c278f71) states 'FFX Chapter 1/3 blocked by a pre-existing, independently-reproducing battle-flow stall ... StrategyGuide never mounts until a decision opens'. FFX Chapter 1 reaches a populated command menu reliably: critic/scratch/builda1-repair/b3-ch1probe.mjs sampled the live battle every ~4.7 s and saw 6 visible command rows (TALK / ATTACK / SPECIAL / WHITE MAGIC / ITEMS / OVERDRIVE) at sample 3, roughly 15 s after the battle screen appeared, and again at samples 7, 9 and 10; the fight then ran to a real defeat at turn 9. The stall is a harness artifact: the waiter only presses Enter when it finds the literal 'ANY KEY' inside a truncated slice of body text, and the BATTLE START banner needs that Enter. Pressing Enter on every poll while no row is visible makes both viewports reach the menu, which is how the failing measurements above were obtained. So the FFX half of the acceptance matrix was reachable and, once run, fails.

PR-0003 PARTIALLY FIXED (major, FFX). The defeat half is genuinely fixed and verified live, but the acceptance clause 'plus any reserve member who took a turn' still fails, and it fails as the same defect the issue is titled after ('a KO'd member vanishes'). Seed sweep on the real engine (Chapter 1, ENEMY_GROUPS_BY_ID['seymour-flux'], gagazetBuild, intendedStrategy, seeds 1-12, critic/scratch/builda1-repair/v6-reserve.test.ts): seed 12 (defeat) — Auron, a reserve member, switched in, completed 14 actions, died on the field, and has NO results row (rows = tidus, yuna, kimahri); seed 8 (victory) — Auron completed 2 actions, KO'd at the end, no row; seed 3 (defeat) — Auron completed 1 action, KO'd at the end, no row. Root cause: src/ui/common/resultsMath.ts:226 still uses the AP-eligibility set as the reserve filter — `const known = [...build.activeSlots, ...build.reserve.filter((id) => earnedIds.has(id))]` — and earnedIds (result.sphereLevelsGained) excludes anyone KO'd at the end per ffx-combat-core.md section 10.1. A reserve member who fought and died is therefore still deleted from the ledger; the fix only rescued members who started in an active slot. The critic's wording is 'a row for each member who was in an active slot at the start plus any reserve member who TOOK A TURN', not 'who earned AP'. The existing unit test at tests/unit/ffx-results-ap.test.ts:181 locks the opposite-but-compatible case (a reserve member switched out on his very first turn, who never completed one, correctly gets no row), so it does not cover this; no test asserts the took-a-turn-then-died case. Suggested smallest fix: track turn participation separately from AP eligibility (result already distinguishes them through results.ts's turnsTaken read) and union that set into `known`, keeping award/levelDelta at 0 for the ineligible.
